question: Why does an undivided sonic nature produce delight and fulfillment?
premises: Where the nature is undivided, it becomes delighting.
This can be observed in rhythmic recitation.
inference: Undivided sonic nature delights because undividedness itself brings fulfillment, as seen in rhythmic recitation.
uncertainties: tālapāṭhataḥ may refer specifically to musical meter, recitative rhythm, or both.
plain_english: When the sound is of an undivided nature, it becomes pleasing; for undividedness brings fulfillment, as can be seen in rhythmic recitation.
